summary: caracas4check ships targeted, XOR-obfuscated RCE payload with persistent.pth interpreter hook
details: The package executes an obfuscated payload both at install time and on every subsequent Python interpreter start. setup.py and c4c_boot.py walk the parent process tree via /proc/<pid>/stat and /proc/<pid>/cmdline to recover the invoking pip's --extra-index-url argument, SHA-256 it against a hardcoded gate hash, and use the URL bytes as an XOR key to decrypt two embedded hex blobs; if the plaintext begins with 'OK\n' it is passed to exec() with the URL bound as variable T. A custom build_py step copies boot.pth and c4c_boot.py into site-packages so the file boot.pth executes 'import c4c_boot' on every Python startup, giving the payload a persistent execution channel independent of whether caracas4check itself is ever imported. The hash-gated URL-keyed decryption is targeted-victim tradecraft: only installers whose pip command line carries the specific --extra-index-url value trigger the payload, and the plaintext cannot be recovered without that value. None of this behavior is consistent with the package's advertised purpose as an API client.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
